main_body: A flat grass ground patch, 4x3 tiles, tiled with a repeating pattern of tufts on a green base
top_band: none (terrain tile, no standing object; the column is a repeating green texture with no top band)
evidence: This is a ground terrain patch, not a standing object, so the 3/4 top-and-front contract does not apply. The column scan shows only grass-tone variation (L 91-136) with no top band or front face structure. Nothing here violates the contract for terrain.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 4 distinct colours and a median of 4 colours per tile. The grass reference has 80 distinct colours and 26 per tile, and the paving reference has 7 distinct colours and 7 per tile. Flat-fill coverage is 19%, against 0% for both references. The surface is a single mid-green base with sparse repeated 1-2px light and dark dots in an obvious tiling pattern, with no clumps and no multi-green blade structure. The pattern repeats every 16px, which reads as mechanical. It is clearly shallower than the Beodeul grass reference.
